ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangle PQRS, P is at the upper left corner, Q is at the lower left corner, S is at the upper right corner, R is at the lower right corner. Point M is located on the left side PQ, and point N is located on the right side SR; the figure draws the diagonal line from P to N and the diagonal line from M to R, and quadrilateral MRNP is enclosed by MP, PN, NR, and RM. Reasoning: The area of rectangle PQRS is 10 square centimeters. Because M and N are respectively the midpoints of PQ and SR, QM and SN are both half of the rectangle's height. The two parts outside quadrilateral MRNP are triangle QMR and triangle PSN. Triangle QMR takes QR as the base, the base length is equal to the rectangle's width, and height QM is equal to half of the rectangle's height, so the area is 1/4 of the entire rectangle's area. Triangle PSN is the same, and the area is also 1/4 of the entire rectangle's area. Therefore the area of quadrilateral MRNP = 10 - 10/4 - 10/4 = 5.

method.method_draft: Use area subtraction from the rectangle. From the image, identify rectangle PQRS with P upper-left, Q lower-left, R lower-right, S upper-right; M lies halfway on left side PQ and N lies halfway on right side SR, and the drawn segments PN and MR bound quadrilateral MRNP. From the text, read that the rectangle area is 10 cm^2 and M,N are midpoints. Since M and N are midpoints, QM and SN are each half the rectangle height. The two outside regions not in MRNP are right triangles QMR and PSN, each with base equal to the rectangle width and height equal to half the rectangle height, so each has area one-fourth of the rectangle. Subtract these two quarter-rectangle triangles from the whole rectangle: area(MRNP) = 10 - 10/4 - 10/4 = 5.
